drafts.title: Authorization of Emergency Use for Four Animal Drugs for the Prevention and Treatment of New World Screwworm; Availability
drafts.summary: FDA issued four Emergency Use Authorizations for animal drugs to prevent or treat New World screwworm infestations in livestock, pets, and some wildlife. The EUAs cover products from Elanco, Zoetis, Bimeda, and Sergeant's, addressing species from cattle and sheep to dogs, cats, and captive cervids. This follows an HHS determination in August 2025 that NWS poses a significant potential public health emergency.
drafts.draft:
Four animal drug EUAs for New World screwworm just dropped in the Federal Register. Prevention and treatment, covering livestock, pets, and some captive wildlife. Four different companies, each with their own authorized product and conditions of use.

I work adjacent to regulatory submissions and clinical data, so the EUA pathway is familiar to me on the human side. Seeing it applied to a screwworm outbreak (and extended to dogs, cats, bison, Sonoran pronghorn) is a good reminder of how much of the same regulatory infrastructure runs underneath veterinary and human health. The species list alone is a lot to track.
